Common cold.description: A mild viral infection of the upper respiratory tract primarily affecting the nose and throat.
self_care: Get plenty of rest and drink abundant warm fluids (broth, herbal teas, warm water).
Use saline nasal drops or steam inhalation to relieve nasal congestion.
Gargle warm salt water (half teaspoon salt in warm water) to soothe throat irritation.
Over-the-counter pain relievers or throat lozenges may provide symptom comfort.
Common cold.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a healthcare provider if symptoms persist beyond 10-14 days, fever exceeds 102°F (39°C), or you develop severe earache or wheezing.
Common cold.precautions: Wash hands frequently, sneeze into elbows or tissues, and avoid close contact with others.

Flu-like illness.description: An acute viral respiratory infection (commonly influenza viruses) causing sudden high fever, chills, and widespread body pain.
self_care: Strict bed rest to help your immune system fight the infection.
Hydrate vigorously with electrolyte solutions, water, and warm soups.
Acetaminophen or Ibuprofen as advised to manage fever and myalgia.
Use a room humidifier to ease breathing.
Flu-like illness.when_to_see_doctor: Seek medical evaluation if experiencing shortness of breath, persistent chest pain, confusion, inability to keep fluids down, or fever returning after initial recovery.
Flu-like illness.precautions: Annual flu vaccination, isolating while symptomatic, wearing masks around high-risk individuals.

COVID-19 like illness.description: A viral syndrome caused by SARS-CoV-2 presenting with respiratory, systemic, and sensory disturbances such as loss of taste or smell.
self_care: Self-isolate to protect family members and the community.
Monitor blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) with a pulse oximeter if available.
Maintain high fluid intake and adequate nutrition.
Rest in prone (belly-down) or semi-upright positions to ease lung expansion.
COVID-19 like illness.when_to_see_doctor: IMMEDIATELY seek emergency care if oxygen saturation drops below 94%, severe shortness of breath occurs, lips or face turn bluish, or persistent chest pressure develops.
COVID-19 like illness.precautions: Take a rapid antigen/RT-PCR test, wear an N95/FFP2 mask, ventilate indoor spaces, and stay updated on vaccinations.

Allergy-like symptoms.description: An immune system hypersensitivity reaction to airborne allergens such as pollen, dust mites, pet dander, or mold spores.
Allergy-like symptoms.duration: Seasonal or chronic depending on allergen exposure
self_care: Identify and minimize exposure to known environmental triggers.
Keep windows closed during high pollen count days and use HEPA air purifiers.
Rinse nasal passages with sterile saline wash or Neti pot.
Non-sedating over-the-counter antihistamines may alleviate sneezing and rhinorrhea.
Allergy-like symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if symptoms interfere with sleep or work, secondary sinus pain develops, or wheezing occurs.
Allergy-like symptoms.precautions: Shower and change clothing after spending extended time outdoors during peak pollen seasons.

Acute Bronchitis.description: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes usually following a viral cold, characterized by persistent chesty cough and congestion.
self_care: Steam inhalation and warm teas with honey to soothe bronchial irritation.
Avoid smoke, fumes, cold dry air, and air pollution.
Rest your voice and body; use elevation while sleeping.
Drink at least 2 to 3 liters of fluids daily to thin bronchial mucus.
Acute Bronchitis.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a physician if coughing produces rust-colored or bloody mucus, wheezing is pronounced, or cough lasts longer than 3-4 weeks.
Acute Bronchitis.precautions: Avoid smoking and secondhand smoke, practice hand hygiene, get vaccinated against respiratory pathogens.

Sinusitis.description: Inflammation or infection of the tissue lining the sinus cavities, causing facial pressure, congestion, and headaches.
self_care: Apply warm, moist compresses to the forehead and cheeks.
Use sterile saline nasal rinses multiple times daily.
Stay hydrated to keep mucus thin and drainage active.
Sleep with your head elevated.
Sinusitis.when_to_see_doctor: Seek care if experiencing severe eye swelling, changes in vision, stiff neck, or symptoms that worsen after initial improvement (double sickening).
Sinusitis.precautions: Treat allergies promptly, avoid cigarette smoke, and use humidifiers during winter.

Strep Throat.description: A bacterial infection caused by Streptococcus pyogenes causing severe throat soreness, pain when swallowing, and sudden fever without cough.
self_care: Gargle warm salt water several times a day.
Drink warm soothing liquids or suck on ice chips.
Eat soft, easy-to-swallow foods like yogurt, soups, and oatmeal.
Complete the entire course of prescribed antibiotics if confirmed bacterial.
Strep Throat.when_to_see_doctor: A rapid strep swab test is essential because untreated strep can lead to rheumatic fever or kidney inflammation. Seek urgent care if difficulty breathing or swallowing saliva occurs.
Strep Throat.precautions: Replace your toothbrush 24-48 hours after starting antibiotics, wash eating utensils thoroughly.

Migraine.description: A neurological condition characterized by intense, throbbing unilateral headache accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light or sound.
self_care: Rest in a quiet, dark, temperature-controlled room.
Apply cold gel packs or warm compresses to the forehead or back of the neck.
Sip small amounts of water or ginger tea to alleviate nausea.
Keep a headache journal to track triggers (stress, skipping meals, caffeine, weather changes).
Migraine.when_to_see_doctor: Seek immediate emergency help if you experience a 'thunderclap' headache (sudden maximum intensity in seconds), confusion, weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking.
Migraine.precautions: Maintain regular sleep schedules, stay hydrated, avoid skipping meals, and manage stress.

Tension Headache.description: The most common type of headache, feeling like a tight band of constant dull ache around the forehead, temples, or back of the head.
self_care: Gentle neck and shoulder stretching exercises.
Take regular screen breaks (follow the 20-20-20 rule).
Stay hydrated and avoid skipping lunch or breakfast.
Apply gentle pressure massage to temples and base of the skull.
Tension Headache.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if headaches occur more than 15 days a month (chronic tension headache) or fail to respond to standard care.
Tension Headache.precautions: Ergonomic desk setup, regular physical activity, stress-reduction techniques like meditation.

Viral Gastroenteritis.description: An intestinal viral infection (stomach flu) causing watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, and vomiting.
self_care: Prioritize oral rehydration solutions (ORS) with small, frequent sips to replace lost electrolytes.
Gradually reintroduce bland foods (BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast).
Avoid dairy, caffeine, alcohol, nicotine, and greasy or highly seasoned foods.
Rest your stomach for a few hours after vomiting before attempting sips of liquid.
Viral Gastroenteritis.when_to_see_doctor: Seek medical attention immediately if unable to keep liquids down for 24 hours, signs of severe dehydration appear (extreme thirst, dry mouth, little/no urination, dizziness), or blood is present in stool/vomit.
Viral Gastroenteritis.precautions: Wash hands with soap and water thoroughly before eating and after using the restroom; disinfect surfaces.

Food Poisoning.description: An illness caused by eating contaminated, spoiled, or toxic food or water, typically presenting rapidly with intense nausea, vomiting, cramps, and diarrhea.
self_care: Hydrate with electrolyte replacement solutions, clear broths, or coconut water.
Rest completely and let the stomach settle.
Do not take anti-diarrheal medications without doctor approval, as they can prevent toxin clearance.
Ease back into eating with crackers, plain rice, and broth.
Food Poisoning.when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care if symptoms include high fever (>102°F), bloody diarrhea, frequent vomiting preventing fluid retention, or neurological symptoms like blurred vision.
Food Poisoning.precautions: Cook meats thoroughly, refrigerate perishables promptly, avoid cross-contamination of raw and cooked foods, check expiration dates.

Acid Reflux / GERD.description: A condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing heartburn, regurgitation, chest discomfort, and throat irritation.
self_care: Eat smaller, more frequent meals rather than large feasts.
Avoid lying down for at least 2 to 3 hours after eating.
Elevate the head of your bed by 6 inches.
Limit trigger foods such as fatty foods, citrus, tomatoes, chocolate, mint, and caffeine.
Acid Reflux / GERD.when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care if chest discomfort is accompanied by radiating jaw or arm pain or shortness of breath. See a doctor if difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) occurs.
Acid Reflux / GERD.precautions: Maintain a healthy body weight, avoid tight-fitting clothing around the waist, quit smoking.

Asthma Flare-up.description: A chronic condition where airways narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus, causing acute episodes of wheezing and breathlessness.
Asthma Flare-up.duration: Hours to days depending on treatment
self_care: Follow your personalized Asthma Action Plan immediately.
Use your quick-relief (rescue) inhaler (e.g., Albuterol) as prescribed.
Sit upright and try to stay calm; practice slow, controlled diaphragmatic breathing.
Remove yourself immediately from identified triggers (cold air, smoke, dust, animal fur).
Asthma Flare-up.when_to_see_doctor: EMERGENCY: Seek immediate emergency medical assistance if rescue inhaler does not bring relief within 15 minutes, you struggle to speak full sentences, or lips/fingernails turn pale or blue.
Asthma Flare-up.precautions: Take daily controller medications as prescribed, track peak flow readings, avoid known triggers.

Allergic Dermatitis.description: An inflammatory skin reaction caused by direct contact with an allergen or substance, resulting in itchy, red, or irritated skin.
self_care: Wash the affected skin gently with mild, fragrance-free soap and lukewarm water.
Apply cool, wet compresses to relieve burning and itching.
Apply hypoallergenic moisturizing lotions or over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream.
Trim fingernails and avoid scratching to prevent secondary bacterial infection.
Allergic Dermatitis.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if rash is widespread, blistered, shows yellow pus (infection), or involves the face or genitals.
Allergic Dermatitis.precautions: Identify contact allergens (poison ivy, nickel, perfumes, latex), wear protective gloves when handling chemicals.

Joint Inflammation / Arthritis.description: Inflammation and swelling of one or more joints causing stiffness, pain, and restricted mobility.
self_care: Balance low-impact physical activity (swimming, cycling, walking) with gentle joint rest.
Apply warm pads for chronic stiffness or ice packs for acute swelling.
Maintain a healthy body weight to reduce stress on weight-bearing joints (knees, hips).
Gentle stretching and mobility exercises daily.
Joint Inflammation / Arthritis.when_to_see_doctor: See a rheumatologist if joint is hot, red, and swollen with sudden fever (possible septic arthritis), or if pain severely limits daily movement.
Joint Inflammation / Arthritis.precautions: Use joint-friendly ergonomic tools, avoid repetitive strain, eat an anti-inflammatory diet rich in omega-3s.

Heat Exhaustion.description: A heat-related illness resulting from prolonged exposure to high ambient temperatures combined with dehydration and physical exertion.
Heat Exhaustion.duration: Few hours to 24 hours with prompt cooling
self_care: Move immediately to a cool, shaded, or air-conditioned environment.
Lie down and elevate legs slightly.
Remove tight, excess, or heavy clothing.
Sip cool water, sports drinks, or rehydration solution (avoid iced drinks which cause stomach cramps).
Apply cool, damp cloths or mist with water and fan vigorously.
Heat Exhaustion.when_to_see_doctor: EMERGENCY: If symptoms worsen, confusion develops, sweating stops despite extreme heat, or body temperature reaches 104°F (40°C), this is Heat Stroke — call emergency services immediately.
Heat Exhaustion.precautions: Stay well hydrated before outdoor activities in hot weather, wear loose lightweight clothing, take breaks in shade.
